title: Travel graph
description: The road/rail network module/blank-inheritance/scripts/core/travel-route.mjs plans a route over, and travel-animation.mjs animates a token along — generated by tools/gazetteer/export_travel_graph.py from tools/city-map's own resolved world (base import + the real ops log replayed), clipped to the visible map content area. Every node is already converted through the map's own georeferencing (tools/gazetteer/core/georef.py) into the campaign map's full-image pixel space (data/map/campaign-map.json's own 12400-square image) — the module does no further coordinate math. Regenerate by re-running that script; never hand-edit.

nodeXy.description: Every node this graph uses, keyed by its OSM node id AS A STRING (JSON object keys always are — travel-route.mjs's own buildAdjacency coerces wayNodes' raw numeric ids to match). Value is [x, y] in campaign-map master-image pixels.

wayNodes.description: Every way (road or rail segment) this graph uses, keyed by its OSM way id as a string — or, since 2026-09-23, a synthetic "gap-<id>" key for a way recovered by derive_gap_graph_from_features (real LineString geometry in the store that never made it into a proper OSM-id-keyed way; see export_travel_graph.py's own docstring). Value is the ordered list of node ids making up that way, as RAW JSON NUMBERS (not strings — the one asymmetry with nodeXy's own keys, verified against a real export and handled once in travel-route.mjs#buildAdjacency rather than by every caller) — a gap-filled way's own node ids are negative synthetic ids minted the same way, never colliding with a real positive OSM node id.

wayClass.description: Added 2026-09-23, same day as core/travel-speed.mjs's own mode-aware hopPlan: every way in wayNodes that citymap/parse.py's RoadGraph.way_class assigned a real OSM highway=*/railway=* tag value to, keyed by the SAME way id (OSM id or synthetic gap-<id>) as wayNodes. Not every way in wayNodes necessarily has an entry — travel-speed.mjs's own modeForWayClass defaults an absent/unknown class to walk rather than guessing a faster mode.

railWayIds.description: Which way ids (a subset of wayNodes' own keys) came from rail specifically, not road — a way tagged with both wins rail in the merge (riding a level crossing is riding the rail line across it), so this is the only way a consumer can tell a way was ridden AS rail rather than happening to also carry a road tag.
